Dodge... Meh. Older ones need a tranny every 120k. Pretty solid motors for the most part. Especially if it has a Cummins. They ride better than Ford's and generally the interior is higher quality. Ever wonder why recently they are so much cheaper than other brands? Look at the VIN. They're made in Mexico. Nearly every single part. Not MAGA.

Chevrolet. My brand of choice. Plenty of power. Sound nice. Ride great. And well built interiors for the most part. Typically not too many powertrain issues. The oil pans gaskets are a pretty common oil leak every once in awhile but that's not too bad. The diesel engines are notorious for blowing head gaskets. That's expensive. My advice when this happens is to put in ARP head studs, problem solved. While you're at it upgrade your turbo and put a tuner in there. I have a buddy who did this and his truck is awesome. Looks like a fleet truck but it is a stupid fast sleeper. 4x4 launcher. Rolls coal on demand too if that's your thing.

For all of these manufacturers they had some serious diesel injector issues for awhile. The kinks have been mostly ironed out so if you're having issues it's time to upgrade.

Toyota. Not too many issues really. Powertrain is the best reliability wise. Decent interiors. I hate the fact that they have solid lifters though. Valve adjustment sucks balls. Surprisingly burned valves almost never happen. I don't like the way they ride though. Gitters.
